title: formation of trapped surfaces for the einstein-euler system
abstract: we prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the einstein--euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. we consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. in particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. to handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. to ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.

title: smooth solutions to the chord log-minkowski problem
abstract: in integral geometry generalized with aleksandrov's variational theory, lutwak-xi-yang-zhang [comm. pure appl. math. 77 (2024)] recently opened the door to researching the cone-chord measures and their log-minkowski problem stemming from the chord integrals, named as the chord log-minkowski problem. in the smooth category, the solvability of the chord log-minkowski problem amounts to dealing with a nonlocal {m}onge-{a}mpère equation involving a riesz potential. in this paper, to study the chord log-minkowski problem, we first present some novel results on the boundary regularity of the riesz potential. based on these results, we obtain the regularity and existence for the chord log-minkowski problem from the perspective of a nonlocal {m}onge-{a}mpère equation and a nonlocal gauss curvature flow equation.

title: stability of the catenoid for the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature equation in 4 spatial dimensions
abstract: we establish the asymptotic stability of the catenoid, as a nonflat stationary solution to the hyperbolic vanishing mean curvature (hvmc) equation in minkowski space $\mathbb{r}^{1 + (n + 1)}$ for $n = 4$. our main result is under a ``codimension-$1$'' assumption on initial perturbation, modulo suitable translation and boost (i.e. modulation), without any symmetry assumptions. in comparison to the $n \geq 5$ case addressed by lührmann-oh-shahshahani arxiv:2212.05620, proving catenoid stability in $4$ dimensions shares additional difficulties with its $3$ dimensional analog, namely the slower spatial decay of the catenoid and slower temporal decay of waves. to overcome these difficulties in the $n = 3$ case, the strong huygens principle, as well as a miraculous cancellation in the source term, plays an important role in arxiv:2409.05968 to obtain strong late time tails. in $n = 4$ dimensions, without these special structural advantages, our novelty is to introduce an appropriate commutator vector field to derive a new hierarchy of estimates with higher $r^p$-weights so that an improved pointwise decay can be established. we expect this to be applicable for proving improved late time tails of other quasilinear wave equations in even dimensions or wave equations with inverse square potential.

title: liouville phenomenon for the klein-gordon equation in 1+1 dimensions
abstract: we study the klein-gordon equation in one spatial and one temporal dimension. physically, this equation describes the wave function of a relativistic spinless boson with positive rest mass. mathematically, this is the most elementary hyperbolic partial differential equation, after the wave equation itself. relative to the origin, the spacetime splits according to the light cones, and we find four quarter-planes, two of which are timelike while the remaining two are spacelike. not unexpectedly, the solutions behave quite differently in the two types of quarter-planes. it turns out that the spacelike quarter-planes exhibit a liouville phenomenon, where insufficient growth forces the solutions to display a certain kind of symmetry, where the values on the two linear edges are in a one-to-one relation. this phenomenon shares features with the classical liouville theorem as well as the phragmen-lindelof principle for harmonic functions. we obtain sharp transition from uniqueness to nonuniqueness.

title: critical semilinear damped wave equations beyond moduli of continuity
abstract: we consider the cauchy problem for semilinear classical damped wave equations with general nonnegative nondecreasing nonlinearities, without imposing a modulus-of-continuity structure or convexity. a dini-type condition expressed directly in terms of the nonlinearity gives small data global in-time existence and extends the nonlinear framework of ebert--girardi--reissig [math. ann. 378 (2020), 1311--1326]. when this integral diverges and the effective total mass of the initial data is positive, convergence of the keller--osserman tail integral is necessary and sufficient for finite-time sobolev blow-up. its divergence gives global grow-up under the same near-zero and mass assumptions.

title: $l^\infty$-regularity thresholds for a generalized gross-pitaevskii equation: dispersive blow-up vs. nonlinear stability
abstract: we study a generalized gross-pitaevskii equation arising in the mean-field description of exciton-polariton bose-einstein condensates. the dynamics close to macroscopic wave functions $r_0e^{iω_0 t +ik_0x}$ is governed by a stabilizing relaxation mechanism without suppressing dispersive blow-up. we show that this competition yields $l^\infty$-regularity thresholds. more precisely, we construct solutions for which arbitrarily small perturbations from $c^4_b$ can develop finite time blow-up in $c^3_b$ whereas perturbations from $c^{4+η}_b$ for every $η>0$, satisfy a global-in-time $c^3_b$-stability estimate. the stability analysis is carried out in modulation spaces $m_{\infty,1}^k$.

title: radiation conditions and uniqueness theorems for open wave-guide networks
abstract: we state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic maxwell equations. to analyze maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the mourre estimates from [29, 32].

title: the $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{r}^n$ with degenerate curvature
abstract: we revisit the $(n-1)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb{r}^n$ proved by the first author in \cite{be-6} and refine the result in the case when the curvature assumptions contain small parameters. the standard $l^p$ estimate is replaced by a more complex norm/quasi-norm of type $\ell^p l^\frac{2}{n-2}$ which reflects the geometry of wave packet propagation and the degenerate curvature assumptions. the primary motivation for this work stems from a concrete application to the study of the quadratic nonlinear schrödinger equation in $\mathbb{r}^{3+1}$, which is done in a companion paper \cite{beboch}.

title: quantitative volume estimate on singular sets of one-phase free boundary problems in ricci limit spaces
abstract: we study limit solutions of the one-phase free boundary problem on noncollapsed ricci limit spaces. we introduce a quantitative stratification $\mathcal{s}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$ of the singular set of the free boundary that simultaneously captures the approximate splitting of the ambient space and the approximate homogeneity and translational invariance of the solution. we also introduce a new truncated parabolic weiss quantity that provides quantitative homogeneity via pinching across scales. although this quantity may not be uniformly bounded across all small scales, it effectively shows that, among the first $j$ scales in a fixed decreasing geometric progression, at most $c\sqrt{j}$ scales fail to exhibit quantitative homogeneity. such slow growth in $j$ enables us to adapt the covering argument of cheeger and naber [arxiv:1103.1819] to show, for every $η>0$, a $cr^{n-k-η}$ upper bound for the volume of the $r$-tubular neighborhood of the $k$-th quantitative singular stratum, $\mathcal{s}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$. the same tubular-neighborhood estimate holds for the effective stratum $\mathcal s_\varepsilon^k$, and in particular we get the minkowski dimension bound $\dim_{\mathcal m} \mathcal s_\varepsilon^k \le k$, from which the previously known sharp bound $\dim_{\mathcal h} \mathrm{sing} \le n-3$ in chan, zhang, and zhu [arxiv:2112.06962] follows. as another corollary, we prove that the free boundary admits a hölder manifold structure away from a set of minkowski dimension at most $n-3$.

title: a quantitative hydrodynamic limit for the vlasov-fokker-planck/navier-stokes system in the fine particle regime
abstract: we justify the hydrodynamic limit of the vlasov-fokker-planck equation coupled with the incompressible navier--stokes equation in the fine regime with a quantitative convergence rate. in this regime, the limiting dynamics is described by the inhomogeneous incompressible navier-stokes system for the fluid-particle mixture. in contrast with the existing relative entropy approaches, the present work extends to a pointwise convergence of the hydrodynamic limits with an explicit rate on any given time interval [0,t]. the proof is based on a macro-micro decomposition around the moving local maxwellian, together with an $\varepsilon$-weighted energy-dissipation structure adapted to the fine particle relaxation scales. furthermore, we remove the classical small background restriction inherent in high-order energy methods, allowing the limiting profile to be possibly large. this is accomplished by exploiting a hidden kelvin-voigt type damped wave equation structure within the macroscopic velocity error system, yielding the critical extra dissipation required to close the uniform estimates.

title: semiclassical band splitting in the infinite chern band model
abstract: we study the two lowest bloch bands of the infinite chern band model in the semiclassical limit. when the berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(π\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the brillouin torus. the proof combines agmon estimates and wkb approximations for a matrix schrödinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. geometric properties of the agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. we provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the berry curvature parameter.

title: spectral theory for schrodinger operators with interface transmission conditions
abstract: interfaces influence transport across biological membranes, habitat boundaries, and composite media. motivated by these applications, we study two classes of schrodinger eigenvalue problems with transmission conditions allowing jumps in the solution or its normal derivative. we develop a weighted variational framework that accommodates asymmetric interface coupling and yields self-adjoint realizations in suitable weighted hilbert spaces. for both problems and their adjoints, we establish discrete spectra, variational eigenvalue characterizations, and eigenfunction completeness in arbitrary spatial dimensions. we prove spectral continuity and identify limiting spectra in singular parameter regimes. we also extend courant's nodal domain theorem to eigenfunctions that may be discontinuous across the interface. the spectral results further extend to divergence-form elliptic operators under suitable assumptions on the coefficients. these results provide a foundation for analyzing elliptic and parabolic equations with interface transmission conditions.

title: recovery of coefficients in a schrödinger system with nonlinear coupling
abstract: we consider the inverse problem of recovering time-dependent coefficients in a system of schrödinger equations with coupled nonlinear terms. we first address the well-posedness of the system for small boundary data and trivial initial data. then, we show that the linearized neumann data stably determines the nonlinear coefficients provided that, at any given time, they are known in some neighborhood of the boundary. the proof relies on linearization and complex geometric optics (cgo) solutions for the linear schrödinger equation. we conclude by outlining an approach based on the direct use of carleman estimates to recover time-independent coefficients in the setting of trivial boundary data but nontrivial initial data.

title: optimizers for the finite-rank fractional lieb--thirring inequality
abstract: the finite-rank fractional lieb--thirring inequality provides an estimate on the riesz sum of the first $n$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional schrödinger operator $(-δ)^s-v$ in terms of the $l^{γ+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb r^d)$ norm of the potential $v$, where the riesz exponent $γ>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. we prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. we further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the euler--lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. in particular, under the condition $γ+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional lieb--thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

title: a sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear schrödinger equations on the real line
abstract: we consider the cauchy problem for semilinear schrödinger equations on the real line. we establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. this criterion is formulated in terms of the mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. to prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the mizohata condition. to prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.

title: the calderón operator for time-harmonic maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
abstract: we consider the time-harmonic maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. we consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $l^\infty$ and the cross section has to be lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. first, we show that the associated calderón operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{h}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_γ;γ) \to \mathbf{h}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_γ;γ)$. second, we consider interior maxwell problems obtained from using the calderón operator and analyze their well-posedness. furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

title: existence and classification of solutions for singular 1-laplacian equations with gradient terms
abstract: we study the existence and qualitative properties of non-negative solutions to singular 1-laplacian problems of the form \begin{equation*}   \begin{cases}   -δ_1 u = g(u)|d u| + h(u)f & \text{in } ω,\newline   u=0 & \text{on } \partialω,   \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $ω\subset \mathbb{r}^n$ is a bounded domain with lipschitz boundary, $0<f\in l^{n,\infty}(ω)$, and $g,h$ are continuous positive functions that may blow up at the origin. we establish the existence of a positive bounded solution even when $g$ is non-integrable at zero and $h(0)=+\infty$, breaking the non-existence phenomenon appearing in the associated $p$-laplacian problems. furthermore, we prove that solutions possess a non-zero boundary trace on a set of positive measure of $\partialω$ whenever $g(s)$ grows sufficiently fast near $s=0$; by contrast, when this growth condition fails, solutions vanishing on the boundary may appear. finally, when $h(0)<+\infty$, we provide a sharp threshold classification of trivial and non-trivial solutions depending on the size of $f$.

title: nonpersistence of full-dimensional tori with polynomial decay in nonlinear schrödinger equations
abstract: we establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear schrödinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+t_vu+μ|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb t:=\mathbb r/(2π\mathbb z). \] for every $κ\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real fourier multiplier $t_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $λ_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the bourgain-type diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_jλ_j,\mathbb z\right) \geqγ_κ\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2κ})^{-1} \] for some $γ_κ>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. for this multiplier, every $3<m<4κ+\frac12$, every $a>0$, and all sufficiently small $μa^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $i_j=a\langle j\rangle^{-m}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $h^1(\mathbb t)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. this advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by kuksin as a main open problem in kam theory for one-dimensional hamiltonian pdes [amer. math. soc. transl. ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, problem 7.1]. bourgain discussed a related question for short-range hamiltonian systems [russian math. surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, section 3]. the proof combines simultaneous diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent fourier coordinates. uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. the mechanism suggests applications to other hamiltonian pdes.

title: cone invariance and homoclinic standing waves for cooperative finite-range dnls equations
abstract: we develop a constrained-power variational framework for positive homoclinic standing waves in one-dimensional discrete nonlinear schrödinger equations with cooperative finite-range interactions. starting from periodic lattices, we construct constrained energy maximizers and use the associated projected gradient flow to establish positive invariance of the cone of nonnegative, even, and unimodal profiles. a central result is that the monotone ordering of the interaction coefficients, \(a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots\ge a_m\ge0\), with \(a_1>0\), provides the structural condition ensuring preservation of this cone under finite-range coupling. under a strict maximum condition above the linear spectral edge, we obtain a uniform frequency gap and period-independent exponential localization. these estimates provide the compactness required for the infinite-period limit and yield positive, even, unimodal, and exponentially localized homoclinic standing waves as strong \(\ell^2(\mathbb z)\)-limits of periodic constrained maximizers. numerical computations for several interaction ranges and cooperative kernels illustrate the effects of extended coupling on dispersion and localization and support the periodic-to-homoclinic convergence predicted by the analysis.

title: transference theory for the trilinear restriction estimate and an application to the quadratic nls in 3d
abstract: in this article we develop a theory for effectively transferring trilinear restriction estimates for the schrödinger equation to functions in a more general resolution space adapted to the schrödinger equation. as an application we provide a global theory for the quadratic nls in three spatial dimensions in the critical sobolev space $\dot{h}^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.

title: gravitational light deflection and shadows in a warm plasma
abstract: analytical studies of light bending in a dispersive medium near compact objects, e.g., black holes or neutron stars, are most challenged by a suitable definition of the medium. the most realistic model would be a hot magnetized plasma. in such a medium, however, an analytical description of light rays is very difficult. therefore, usually an isotropic dispersive medium is assumed in analytical calculations. while it is possible to formulate equations for a general refractive index, which some studies do, most attention in the literature is given to the particular case of a cold, non-magnetized electron-ion plasma. whereas this model covers many astrophysically relevant situations, there are indications that in some cases the plasma temperature is so high that the approximation of a cold plasma is no longer valid. for this reason, we consider in this paper a warm, non-magnetized electron-ion plasma, where the temperature is not set equal to zero but assumed to be small enough, such that relevant equations can be linearized with respect to it. after discussing the general equations for light rays in such a medium on a general-relativistic spacetime, we specify to the axially symmetric and stationary case which includes the spherically symmetric and static case. in particular, we calculate the influence of a warm plasma on the bending angle. in the spherically symmetric and static case, we also calculate the shadow in a warm plasma. we illustrate the general results with a static (respectively corotating) and an infalling warm plasma on schwarzschild and kerr spacetimes.

title: modeling the merger-ringdown of an eccentric test-mass inspiral into a kerr black hole using the effective-one-body framework
abstract: we characterize and phenomenologically model the merger-ringdown of gravitational waves emitted by a small compact object that plunges and merges into a kerr black hole from equatorial-eccentric inspirals. the waveforms are generated employing a time-domain teukolsky code sourced with trajectories computed using the effective-one-body framework. we span values of the kerr spin $a\in[-0.9, 0.9] $, eccentricity at the last stable orbit (lso) $ e_{\rm lso} \in [0,0.9] $, and relativistic anomaly $ ξ_{\rm lso} \in [0 , 2 π]$. we characterize the last peak of the waveform and ringdown features across the parameter space, finding that the eccentricity mainly affects the last peak features, while it has a smaller impact on the ringdown signal. in contrast, the relativistic anomaly measured at the lso influences the morphology of the last peak in a restricted portion of the parameter space and has no impact on the ringdown part. we perform the analysis for all the spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes normally included in the $\texttt{seobnr}$ family of models, $(\ell,m)\in\{ (2,2), (3,3), (4,4), (5,5), (2,1), (3,2), (4,3)\}$. finally, we introduce a merger-ringdown model for $\texttt{seob-tmle}$, a forthcoming inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform model for eccentric spin-aligned binary black holes in the test-mass limit, whose features can be extended to comparable-mass regimes. the model also accounts for quasinormal mode mixing during the ringdown. it provides a first step toward incorporating the impact of residual eccentricity close to merger into spin-aligned effective-one-body merger-ringdown models for binary black holes.

title: radial oscillations of viscous stars
abstract: oscillation modes of neutron stars, a key target for third-generation gravitational wave detectors, encode key information about their constituent nuclear matter. in this work, we study the effect of viscosity on oscillations of cold, polytropic, spherically symmetric neutron stars. we focus on purely radial oscillations and work perturbatively to linear order within two hydrodynamic frameworks: the acausal covariant generalization of the navier-stokes equations proposed by eckart, and the causal generalization formulated by bemfica, disconzi, noronha, and kovtun (bdnk). we find that viscosity damps the radial modes on millisecond timescales and induces fractional shifts in the oscillation frequency which increase both with the compactness and viscosity of the star, reaching up to the percent level for the fundamental mode with bulk viscosities $ζ\sim10^{30}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. for more viscous stars, the oscillation frequency decreases, becoming zero (i.e., an overdamped mode) for $ζ\gtrsim10^{31}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. we also study the linear threshold of gravitational collapse. consistent with recent analytic results in the zero heat conductivity limit, we find that viscosity in eckart theory cannot stabilize an unstable inviscid star. we provide numerical evidence that viscosity in bdnk theory is similarly unable to prevent gravitational collapse, but it slightly modifies the threshold of collapse. overall, our results advance our understanding of the impact of viscosity on the oscillation modes of neutron stars, a key component of viscous asteroseismology with next-generation gravitational wave detectors.

title: analytical solutions for timelike orbits around damour-solodukhin wormholes
abstract: we investigate timelike geodesics around damour-solodukhin wormholes, which are schwarzschild-like geometries characterized by a deformation parameter $λ$ that determines the radius of the throat, $r_{\rm th}$. the radial potential admits four roots, including the throat radius itself, allowing the throat to merge with other roots and form double, triple, and quartic degeneracies. triple-root configurations associated with the throat, in principle, can determine the innermost stable circular orbit (isco), which provides a potential observational distinction from schwarzschild black holes. using the mino-time parametrization, we derive particle trajectories with closed-form analytical solutions in terms of incomplete elliptic integrals for both bound and unbound motion. our focus is on the location of double or triple roots at the throat, where the azimuthal angle and coordinate time of orbital motion show logarithmic or power-law divergence as the particle approaches the throat. by contrast, trajectories remain regular when the throat corresponds to a simple root, allowing particles to traverse smoothly between the two asymptotically flat regions. we also derive exact homoclinic solutions associated with the throat and compute the corresponding lyapunov exponent. in addition, inspiral and plunge trajectories through the throat are analyzed. these results provide analytic insights into the particle dynamics and possible observational signatures of the wormholes.

title: extended parameterized spin expansion formalism for ringdown analysis with gw250114
abstract: parameterized descriptions of black-hole quasinormal-mode spectra are essential for testing gravity with ringdown observations. we extend the parameterized spin expansion coefficients (parspec) formalism by simultaneously sampling the characteristic length scale $\tilde{\ell}$ and the scaling index $\tilde{p}$, rather than fixing $\tilde{p}$ to a theory-motivated integer and constraining $\tilde{\ell}$. physically, this extension promotes the scaling of the spectral corrections coming from higher-curvature operators to an observable quantity. methodologically, it enables us to investigate the enlarged parspec parameter space and identify the prior geometry induced by conditions on the effective coupling $γ$. we examine the robustness of the framework by using the $220$ and $220+221$ ringdown models over different start times with informative priors on mass and luminosity for gw250114, and further study a joint constraint with gw231123. we pointed out that $γ<1$ avoids an artificial correlation between $\tilde{p}$ and $\tilde{\ell}$ among the coupling prescriptions considered, and the choices of ringdown starting time and qnm mode content in the parspec framework should be matched to the information content and resolving power of the data. higher-snr ringdowns and hierarchical analyses of a larger event population will be required to break the $\tilde{p}$-$\tilde{\ell}$ degeneracy and directly probe the scaling structure of corrections to gr.

title: quadrupole and quadratic-in-spin effects in quasicircular, spinning, asymmetric binaries
abstract: next-generation gravitational-wave detectors will require significant improvements in current theoretical waveform models, particularly in the case of asymmetric-mass binaries. here we provide one such improvement by calculating fully relativistic finite-size effects for small mass ratios -- primarily, fluxes of energy -- including quadratic-in-secondary-spin terms, spin-induced quadrupole terms, and tidally induced quadrupole terms, for quasicircular inspirals of a small companion into a kerr black hole. we formulate these calculations within a multiscale waveform-generation framework in self-force theory, which could be used, with an energy-balance law we derive, to develop self-contained waveform models for asymmetric binaries involving stars orbiting black holes. our results could additionally be used to improve other families of waveform models across all mass ratios. we present results both as complete numerical data sets on a chebyshev grid and as analytical post-newtonian expansions (to sixth pn order relative to the leading term in each contribution to the flux).

title: co-design of ground-based gravitational wave detector networks
abstract: discussions around the design philosophy and location of the next generation of ground-based gravitational wave detectors are still underway. in this context, we propose ifoscout, an innovative methodology for detector co-design based on state-of-the-art machine-learning (ml) techniques. as a simple demonstration, we present a two-stage simulation of a network of fictional l-shaped interferometers whose sensitivity is optimized within physical and geographical constraints, indirectly resulting in reducing the costs. to achieve this, we gather publicly available data for two token locations and establish the length and orientation with reinforcement learning (rl). next, we optimize the internal detector parameters related to cavity stability to achieve the best possible sensitivity by means of differential programming (dp). we make the case that pipelines such as ifoscout could have a positive impact on the final design of new generation detectors (e.g. the einstein telescope, the cosmic explorer, etc.), given precise data and detailed, realistic simulations of the interferometers.

title: static electric and magnetic traversable wormholes in $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: every traversable wormhole reported so far in static (2+1) gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics has come from a power-maxwell lagrangian l propto |f|^k restricted to k=1/2, always forcing the cosmological constant to a fixed sign or zero. we show these restrictions are artefacts of that single choice, not physical requirements, and give a complete classification of static traversable wormholes in this theory. of the three mutually exclusive electromagnetic configurations compatible with the symmetry, the radial electric branch admits no throat for any lagrangian or lambda. in each remaining branch, azimuthal electric and magnetic, the field equations admit exactly two regimes: either the redshift function is fixed, leaving the shape function b(r) completely free with lambda absorbed without constraint; or the redshift is generic, in which case b(r) becomes fixed instead. we solve both regimes in closed form in both branches, and show that fixing the lagrangian to any single power k forces lambda nonzero and determines b(r) up to finitely many constants: this freedom requires the lagrangian to be genuinely unrestricted. one azimuthal-electric family reproduces the static btz mass function, turning the vacuum black hole into a wormhole once sourced by the nonlinear field. applied to the unique conformal power-maxwell theory, k=3/4, previously known only as a radial-branch charged black hole, the same lagrangian yields genuine wormholes in the azimuthal and magnetic branches, showing the electromagnetic configuration, not the lagrangian, decides between a horizon and a throat; born-infeld electrodynamics admits no throat in any branch.

title: towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
abstract: near the threshold between scattering and capture by a schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. the fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. using the wentzel, kramers, and brillouin (wkb) approximation to solve the regge-wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. we then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. we further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in kerr. interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. more broadly, our work illustrates how wkb methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.

title: all order gravitational wave tails for subleading post-newtonian expansion
abstract: the low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. in the newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. at the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in newton's constant $g$. we extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. we consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. the correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. for $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arxiv:2610.07134.

title: optimal strategies for gravitational-wave memory detection with noise marginalization in pulsar timing arrays
abstract: current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. in order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for gw memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. we additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. we perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the nanograv $15$-year data set. we find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the nanograv $15$-year comparisons. we conclude that for realistic ptas the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.

title: exact ads and pp-waves in multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions
abstract: we construct exact anti-de sitter (ads) waves and pp-waves in ghost-free multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions for an arbitrary number $\mathcal{n}$ of vielbeins, in any spacetime dimension $d\geq3$. deforming proportional ads and minkowski solutions along a common null direction reduces the full nonlinear field equations to coupled linear differential equations for the wave profiles, without restricting their amplitudes. the system is diagonalised in the same eigenbasis as the perturbative fierz-pauli mass matrix, separating the solutions into one massless and $\mathcal{n}-1$ massive eigenprofiles. we obtain explicit radial and transverse solutions and impose an ads boundary falloff. this falloff admits the appropriate radial branch of every mode with non-negative squared mass and excludes profiles with negative squared masses, including logarithmic solutions at the breitenlohner-freedman threshold. we also relate the ads waves to pp-waves through a local flat limit. explicit examples exhibit wave configurations that cannot be reproduced by ghost-free pairwise theories, demonstrating that genuine multi-field interactions support new exact gravitational-wave solutions.

title: quantum-corrected and hairy black holes via analogue gravity
abstract: this thesis maps two exotic black-hole geometries onto the transonic flow of a de laval nozzle and reads their perturbative response in aerodynamic variables. the first is the hairy black hole of gravitational decoupling, constrained by the dominant energy condition and by the existence of a horizon. the second is the calmet-kuipers metric, short-ranged and governed by the single wilson coefficient of the dimension-six operator that the two-loop goroff-sagnotti divergence identifies. perturbations of spin 0, 1/2, 1 and 2 reduce to a schrödinger-type wave equation, whose spectrum the mashhoon method returns as a whole overtone tower in closed form, every frequency damped. the two corrections are distinguished by which channel responds and by how strongly all of them do, the quantum coupling moving the quality factor by up to 37% in the scalar and dirac channels and by about 10% in the other two, while the hair acts on every channel alike. identifying the two tortoise coordinates turns the equality of the potentials into a sturm-liouville problem, so that the prescribed barrier fixes the wall profile and with it the flow variables and the thrust coefficient. the hair is felt across the whole divergent section, whereas the quantum correction registers only near the throat and grows as the inverse fourth power of the mass, which confines it to primordial black holes. the analogy is kinematical, so the duct reproduces the scattering of perturbations off these geometries without reproducing the field equations behind them.

title: axial gravitational quasinormal modes of magnetically charged black holes
abstract: in this paper, we consider axial perturbations on the magnetically charged string-inspired euler-heisenberg black hole. since axial metric perturbation decouples from axial electromagnetic perturbation, here we mainly focus on axial gravitational perturbation. by using wkb approximation and aim methods, we make a detailed analysis of the gravitational quasinormal frequencies by varying the characteristic parameters of gravitational perturbation and black holes. it is found these results obtained through the aim method are in good agreement with those of obtained by wkb method, including these results extracted from the time-domain profiles. the greybody factor is calculated by wkb method. the effects of these parameters $q_m$, $ε$ and multipole number $l$ on the greybody factor are also studied.

title: quantum cosmology in page-wootters' framework: singularity resolution and clock coherence
abstract: we investigate the fate of big-bang singularity and coherence between distinct clock states in a quantum cosmological setting within the page-wootters framework. with a canonically quantized plane-symmetric bianchi i universe, we employ dirac factorization of the wheeler-dewitt constraint and obtain a schrodinger-like equation which is first-order in an internal clock variable. by constructing its solution as a gaussian wave packet in the expanding branch, we derive the corresponding conditional state and probability density of the universe. we find that the conditional probability density vanishes in the zero-volume limit, indicating resolution of the big-bang singularity within this probabilistic framework. another prespective of the study is provided by the construction of density matrix from the conditional states associated with different clock readings and the remaining degree of freedom. by tracing out the remaining subsystem, we obtain the reduced density matrix and analyze the resulting coherence as a function of separation between different clock states. these results provide a relational characterization of singularity resolution and demonstrate how the spectral properties of the quantum state govern the temporal coherence between different clock states in the page-wootters description.

title: numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
abstract: a confident detection of orbital eccentricity in gravitational-wave signals from black hole-neutron star systems would be a strong indicator of their dynamical formation origin. while eccentric waveform models have recently been developed, their validity for analyzing black hole--neutron star signals has yet to be tested against numerical-relativity simulations. building upon our previous study of quasicircular black hole--neutron star mergers, we perform simulations of a subset of these systems with orbital eccentricities around five times larger than those inferred for gw200105_162426. additionally, we perform simulations with magnetized matter to assess whether trapped $g$-mode oscillations persist in strongly magnetized disks. regarding the emitted gravitational-wave signal, we find that the effective one-body waveform model seobnrv5ehm shows reasonable agreement unless tidal contributions become important, and the inspiral-only post-newtonian models pyefpe/pyefpehm show larger disagreement in the late inspiral. for the equal-mass system, which has the largest effective tidal deformability, eccentric tidal corrections have a small but noticeable impact on the phase, $\sim0.1$ rad. we find an almost negligible impact of eccentricity on the properties of the remnant black hole, and differences of up to a factor of two in the remnant disk mass. trapped $g$ modes in the accretion disks have the same frequency regardless of the eccentricity, confirming that they depend mainly on the properties of the remnant black hole. we find that when accretion disks are strongly magnetized, they become less dense and have less pronounced structure, and that the trapped $g$ modes previously identified in the unmagnetized cases are efficiently damped.

title: from cosmic bounces to primordial black holes: the role of primordial magnetic fields
abstract: we investigate primordial black hole (pbh) formation from primordial magnetic fields generated during a non-singular ekpyrotic bounce. a time-dependent coupling between the electromagnetic field and a scalar background breaks conformal invariance and amplifies gauge field fluctuations during contraction, generating magnetic fields whose anisotropic stress dominates during radiation domination. by retaining finite-wavenumber cutoffs, we compute the ultraviolet-dominated curvature spectrum, evaluate density-perturbation variance, and determine pbh abundances using both monochromatic and critical-collapse prescriptions. for benchmark parameters, the critical collapse mass spectrum peaks at $m\simeq 2.0\times10^{-3}m_\odot$ , with a total pbh dark matter fraction of $f_{pbh}\approx 10^{-5}$, forming a subdominant subsolar pbh population. enforcing the cosmological overclosure bound ($f_{\mathrm{pbh}} \le 1$) constrains the primary background parameters, namely the end-of-contraction hubble scale ($h_{\mathrm{end}} \le 1.6 \times 10^3~\mathrm{gev}$) and the contraction exponent ($q \le 0.247$), establishing a physical boundary consistent with the electromagnetic backreaction limit. shifting to asteroid-mass pbhs or a larger dark matter fraction requires modifying the ultraviolet cutoff and contraction duration. this analysis highlights the essential role of finite-wavenumber cutoffs and assumed-collapse prescriptions in linking bounce magnetogenesis to the predicted pbh abundance.

title: an exact simpson-visser family in bumblebee gravity
abstract: we construct an exact simpson-visser solution in metric bumblebee gravity, supported by a phantom scalar, magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics, and a spacelike configuration of fixed norm. the independent vector equation determines a local lagrange multiplier and a temporal component that permits a regular ingoing extension across metric horizons. reconstruction of the matter functions identifies a continuous family of wormholes, null minimum geometries, and black-bounces within one action. in the black hole case, the areal photon sphere and critical timelike orbit radii retain their schwarzschild values, whereas angular deflection, periapsis advance, and photon orbit instability depend on the bounce and bumblebee parameters. the metric shadow coincides with the schwarzschild prediction at fixed lapse mass and areal observer position; in addition, the adopted sgr a* shadow diameter and m87* angular mass comparisons do not determine these parameters separately. the coupled axial equations yield distinct tensor, metric, and transverse bumblebee characteristics. we compute fundamental auxiliary massless scalar and ordinary maxwell probe resonances by chebyshev spectral collocation and estimate the tensor and bumblebee resonance scales at leading geometric optics order. nonnegative probe potentials exclude exponentially growing probe modes. for negative nonminimal coupling and a nonzero temporal case, however, the supporting electromagnetic field develops an angular gradient instability in its extraordinary polarization. the unstable characteristic persists in the coupled principal symbol, while a variational construction establishes growing modes on the fixed geometry and lower bounds on their growth rates.

title: thermodynamics of rotating black holes with constrained primary hair
abstract: an exact rotating geometry need not define a black hole in equilibrium when its surface gravity varies across the horizon. we construct an asymptotically flat, non-kerr subfamily of the aligned null solutions of generalized proca theory whose outer horizon is exactly killing and isothermal to second order in rotation. the horizon conditions constrain the vector hair, and integrability of the normalized horizon charge fixes the remaining second-order amplitude. computing the complete gravitational and nonminimal vector surface charges, we obtain the asymptotically normalized mass and total angular momentum, and derive a logarithmic hamiltonian entropy. the first law holds in both independent directions of the resulting two-parameter solution space. we express the mass as a function of entropy and angular momentum, recover the geometric thermodynamic potentials, and establish a scale-corrected smarr relation that retains the dimensionful coupling. the exact metric defines the geometry, while equilibrium thermodynamics is consistently restricted to second order in spin.

title: photon-return and polar-focusing crossovers near extremal kerr
abstract: how precisely must a photon's impact parameter be tuned for it to complete $n$ windings around a nearly extremal kerr black hole before escaping, and how does the same near extremal scaling control the focusing of neighboring rays? for equatorial prograde returns we find, with $κ=\sqrt{1-a^2/m^2}$ and $x=nκ$, $ε_n=\sqrt{3}\,κ/(e^{2πx}-1) +o(κ^2|\lnκ|)$. this single law connects the extremal inverse-winding hierarchy to subextremal exponential accumulation. perturbing the return family quasi-equatorially, we derive a second scaling law for the polar jacobi phase, $ψ_θ=2\ln[\sinh(πx)/κ]+c_s+o(1)$, and show that its focusing points cross from geometric spacing in winding number to asymptotically uniform spacing $δ\mathcal n\simeq(2κ)^{-1}$. numerical integrations of the exact kerr radial dynamics and linear polar equation verify both scaling collapses. thus near extremal kerr exhibits parametrically distinct winding and polar-focusing scales, rather than a discontinuous jump between extremal and subextremal lensing hierarchies.

title: from accelerating rotating black holes to a swirling universe
abstract: we demonstrate that the swirling universe can be recovered through a coordinated horizon-degeneration and scaling procedure applied to the kerr c-metric. the construction exploits the horizon structure of accelerating, rotating black holes, which allows their inner and outer horizons to coalesce while simultaneously approaching the acceleration horizon. by magnifying the near-acceleration-horizon region faster than the black hole horizons approach it, the pair of accelerating, rotating black holes is pushed to an infinite proper distance, while a finite gravitomagnetic twist survives. the resulting geometry reproduces precisely the swirling universe, providing a physical interpretation of its intrinsic rotation as the gravitational remnant of rotating black holes sent to infinity.

title: universality classes, thermodynamics of group entropies, and black holes
abstract: conventional boltzmann--gibbs statistical mechanics successfully describes systems with weak to moderate correlations, in which the number of accessible configurations $w(n)$ grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom $n$. however, this framework breaks down for systems for which the effectively occupied configuration space exhibits non-exponential growth. while numerous generalized entropies have been proposed to address this limitation, a coherent link to classical thermodynamic laws has remained elusive. here, we propose group entropies as a unifying framework, defining universality classes of entropies through the asymptotic scaling of $w(n)$, each yielding an extensive entropy. we show that this approach provides the basis for a consistent thermodynamic formulation beyond the boltzmann--gibbs paradigm. in particular, by expressing these entropies in terms of thermodynamic state variables, we demonstrate their consistency with classical thermodynamics, in close analogy to the emergence of the clausius entropy from the boltzmann--gibbs formalism. focusing on the zeroth thermodynamic law, we identify the empirical temperature and, by using carathéodory's formulation of the second law, we derive the associated absolute temperature. as an application, we analyse black-hole thermodynamics using the extensive group entropy class corresponding to stretched-exponential behaviour of $w(n)$ and derive a negative heat capacity, known to be a hallmark property of black holes. this result holds for the stretched-exponential entropies associated with both the bekenstein--hawking and barrow entropy scalings.

title: hidden symmetry group for particle orbits (timelike geodesics) in schwarzschild spacetime
abstract: for the timelike geodesic equations in schwarzschild spacetime, three hidden conserved quantities were found recently, which are analogues of dynamical quantities related to the well-known laplace--runge--lenz (lrl) vector in newtonian gravity. in particular, the geodesic equations possess an lrl angle, an lrl killing-vector time and an lrl proper time, each of which is a (piecewise) conserved quantity for all timelike geodesics. the present work provides a natural symmetry interpretation for these three quantities by applying noether's theorem in reverse to the geodesic lagrangian. this yields three new (hidden) lrl symmetry transformations. unlike the killing symmetries, which constitute point transformations on the geodesic configuration variables and close without the use of the geodesic equations, the new symmetries are dynamical transformations which essentially involve the geodesic momenta variables and close only on solutions of the geodesic equations. the commutator structure of the lrl symmetries is shown to depend on whether a geodesic is bounded or not, and horizon-crossing or not, while their physical meaning is connected to their action on the geodesic energy and angular momentum. together with the killing symmetries and re-parameterization symmetries of the geodesics lagrangian, they generate the complete noether symmetry group of the timelike geodesic equations.

title: modal bases of coaxial electromagnetic step index fibers
abstract: we consider the eigenvalue problem to find the modes of an electromagnetic coaxial step index fiber. more specific, we consider a closed (meaning pec boundary conditions) cylindrical waveguide with circular cross section $γ$, wave propagation modeled by the time-harmonic maxwell's equations with frequency $ω$, the permeability $μ$ and the permittivity $ε$ being scalar, uniformly positive, piece-wise constant and depending only on the radial variable of the cross section. we prove that if the deviation from the homogeneous case is small, i.e., $δ_{ε,μ}:=\|ε-ε_0\|_{l^\infty}+\|μ-μ_0\|_{l^\infty}<<1$, then the (appropriately scaled) tangential electric (magnetic) fields of the modes form riesz bases in $\mathbf{h}_{0}(\operatorname{curl}_γ;γ)$ ($\mathbf{h}(\operatorname{curl}_γ;γ)$) and the natural trace space $\mathbf{h}_{0}^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_γ;γ)$ ($\mathbf{h}^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_γ;γ)$). these results hold also for complex frequencies $ω$. in addition, if $ω\in\mathbb{r}$, then for small enough $δ_{ε,μ}$ all wavenumbers are located on the axes and there exist no backward modes. key tools in the analysis are a particular reformulation of the eigenvalue problem, the perturbation theory for selfadjoint operators under a local subordinate condition and uniform properties of bessel functions.

title: ideal gårding polynomials
abstract: we introduce ideal gårding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of gårding polynomials whose gårding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. this class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the lorentzian class.   our main result is that ideal gårding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. a key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate gårding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of pitman--stanley polytopes. we establish quotient concavity, and newton--maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and lorentzian polynomials.

title: singular stochastic heat equations with fractional memory
abstract: we extend the paracontrolled distribution approach of gubinelli, imkeller, and perkowski to singular stochastic heat equations with caputo fractional time derivatives. by establishing schauder estimates for the time-fractional heat flow and controlling history terms, we address the difficulties arising from temporal memory and the lack of the semigroup property. for the one-dimensional rough burgers-type equation driven by space-time white noise with spatial dissipation \((-δ)^σ\), we prove global well-posedness for \(σ\in(5/6,1]\) and \(ν\in(6σ/(12σ-5),1]\). for the heat equation with nonlinear multiplicative spatial white noise on the two-dimensional torus, we establish local well-posedness of renormalized solutions and an \(l^\infty\) blow-up criterion for every \(ν\in(0,1]\).

title: classification of boundary blow-ups for the mumford-shah functional with dirichlet boundary conditions
abstract: we classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the mumford-shah functional on bounded planar domains with dirichlet boundary conditions. at every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. this settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

title: cavity collapse and kinetic energy concentration in three-dimensional free-boundary euler flow
abstract: we construct smooth axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary euler equations in bounded domains for which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at a finite time $t$. the velocity has a single-valued potential, and the construction applies without surface tension and with any fixed positive surface tension. both boundary components remain embedded and disjoint before collapse, while the outer boundary converges smoothly. the terminal outer meridional domain may be any smooth bounded simply connected domain whose closure is separated from the rotation axis; the interior point generating the collapse circle and the positive concentrated energy may be prescribed independently. we prove a sharp collapse law with radius asymptotic to an explicit multiple of $(t-t)^{1/2}|\log(t-t)|^{-1/4}$, determine curvature blow-up asymptotics, and show that kinetic energy concentrates uniformly on the circle. for a canonical reflection symmetric family, we identify a common cylindrical spacetime limit and sharp velocity and pressure profiles. at every fixed spatial point in the region enclosed by the limiting outer boundary and away from the collapse circle, the velocity tends to zero while the pressure tends to positive infinity. for this family, we characterize the topology of the limiting material map and prove its optimal $1/2$-hölder regularity and sharp $w^{1,p}$ threshold $1\le p<2$, with first derivatives in weak $l^2$ but not in $l^2$. these canonical solutions admit weak continuations that preserve mass and momentum and whose total energy drops at collapse by exactly the concentrated kinetic energy.

title: three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
abstract: the three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by qing and tian [comm. pure appl. math. 1997]. we extend this method to a class of $(τ,ε)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. these inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. in the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of rivière's equation, $α$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and willmore surfaces.

title: scattered light noise due to dust particles contamination in the vacuum pipes of the einstein telescope
abstract: high-sensitivity optical measurements such as those performed in interferometric gravitational wave detectors are prone to scattered light noise. to minimize it, optical components must meet tight requirements on surface roughness and bulk defects. nonetheless, the effectiveness of these measures can be undermined by other sources of scattered light. in this article, we examine scattered light noise caused by particles deposited on surfaces, especially on the baffles inside the vacuum pipes of the einstein telescope's interferometer arms. first, we study light scattering by particles deposited on a surface and having diameters from about one tenth to hundred times the light wavelength: we discuss its angular distribution and dependence on particle size and refractive index, and on polarization. then, we specialize to the case of the einstein telescope arms and quantify the maximum allowed density of particles on each arm baffle. we conclude with cleanliness guidelines for the assembly of the vacuum pipes, including the required cleanliness class of the installation environment.

title: chaotic imprints in gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio-inspirals embedded in dark matter halo
abstract: we investigate imprints of chaos in gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals configuration, where a stellar massive object, confined in an external potential as a harmonic oscillators, orbits a supermassive schwarzschild-like black hole embedded in a dehnen-type dark matter halo. in our previous work (das s, et al., extreme-mass-ratio inspirals embedded in dark matter halo: existence of homoclinic orbit and horizon-induced chaos, sci. china-phys. mech. astron. 69, 290413 (2026)), we demonstrated the system's transition from non-chaotic to chaotic dynamics by analyzing poincaré sections, orbital evolution, and lyapunov exponents across different energies and dark matter halo parameters. in this work, we compute the gravitational waveforms of the small celestial object along different chaotic and non-chaotic orbits by implementing the numerical kludge scheme. we further perform spectral analysis of the gravitational waveforms from such orbits. in particular, we show that when the system is in a chaotic state, the gravitational wave signals are characterized by broader frequency spectra with finite widths, irregular waveform modulations with comparatively large strain excursions for the chaotic trajectories considered here, together with modified energy-emission characteristics, distinctly differentiating them from the signals generated during the system's non-chaotic state. furthermore, we discuss the potential detectability of these orbits for upcoming observatories like laser interferometer space antenna (lisa), tianqin, and taiji, emphasizing the significant potential for detecting chaotic imprints in gravitational waves to substantially enhance our understanding of chaotic dynamics in black hole physics and the dark matter environments of galactic nuclei.

title: self-resonance preheating in deformed attractor models: oscillon formation and evolution
abstract: it is well known that, in potentials that are quadratic near the minimum but shallower away, such as small-$α$ ($α\ll m_p^2$) attractors, the inflaton condensate fragments into localized compact objects known as oscillons during self-resonance preheating. in this work, we investigate self-resonance in a deformed $α$-attractor t-model with a gaussian feature near the minimum, distant from the end of inflation. linear analysis reveals altered resonance bands and deformed floquet charts dependent on feature parameters, primarily through the localized modification of $v''(ϕ)$. in fully nonlinear lattice simulations, we find that the potential feature has only a modest influence on gradient-energy transfer during resonance, whereas the subsequent evolution becomes strongly dependent on the gaussian feature's dimensionless amplitude $h$. increasing $|h|$ suppresses the formation and persistence of compact oscillons, resulting in fewer objects and a smaller fraction of energy stored in them. the total-energy and internal-gradient-energy diagnostics give consistent lifetime trends. within the directly resolved range, the oscillon lifetime decreases nonlinearly with increasing $|h|$, with negative $h$ generally producing shorter lifetimes than positive $h$ of the same magnitude. the gravitational wave emission is dominated by the resonant stage and becomes strongly suppressed after oscillon formation. we further find an enhancement in the high-frequency tail of the spectrum, sourced by the potential feature. although a complete reheating description requires external couplings and higher-resolution simulations, clear qualitative differences in the post-inflationary expansion history already emerge within our simulated time window. these results clarify how potential features affect preheating dynamics and oscillon evolution.

title: strong lensing and quasinormal modes of a black hole with a global monopole
abstract: in this paper, we investigate various key aspects of a static and spherically symmetric black hole with a global monopole. firstly, we analyze the deflection angle in the strong field limit of a spacetime with a global monopole. it shows that the angle of deflection increases when the two characteristic parameters for the monopole configuration, $η$ and $λ$, increase. the influence of the global monopole parameter on the lensing observables and the black hole shadow is studied. this shows that a larger monopole parameter corresponds to larger shadow radii. the dynamics of timelike geodesics is also investigated in the spacetime. general circular orbits and the innermost stable circular orbits (isco) of timelike particles are discussed, highlighting that the monopole parameter significantly affects the circular orbits and the isco. in particular, it is observed that the radius of isco rises monotonically with $η$. in addition, the lyapunov exponent is used to analyze the stability of timelike geodesics. we also determine the quasinormal modes under electromagnetic perturbations for different values of $η$. our findings indicate that increasing the monopole parameter gives rise to electromagnetic perturbations with more slowly damped oscillations. to further validate the derived quasinormal mode spectrum, we discuss the time-domain evolution of the perturbation, confirming the presence of the characteristic quasinormal ringing followed by late-time power-law tails. finally, comparison with the eht observations of m87* and sgr a* determines the parameter combinations of $η$ and $λ$ compatible with current observations, and the observational prospects of the strong-lensing observables are discussed.

title: cracking gravitational wave multiple ringdown modes in space
abstract: ringdown signals from perturbed black holes (bhs) offer a clean window into bh spacetime, strong-field gravity, and fundamental physics. presently the quasi-normal modes of stellar-mass bh ringdowns have been successfully extracted in the ground-based gravitational wave (gw) observations. looking ahead, the future space-borne observatories will listen to the ringdowns from massive bh binary coalescences more loudly and resolve multiple modes to unprecedented precision, which calls for efficient approaches to mitigate the sharply increasing computational burden. we develop a practical ringdown analysis pipeline for space-borne detectors by implementing firefly, a novel acceleration algorithm validated in ground-based detectors, and for the first time demonstrate its compatibility and effectiveness with the time-delay interferometry (tdi) observables. with high fidelity, we achieve an over two-order-of-magnitude speedup for a simulated ringdown signal including six modes, providing a viable and scalable route for multi-mode ringdown analysis in the space context. this new approach has sound statistical interpretation and is extensible to other gw sources in band.

title: ir behaviour of one-loop complex $\mathbb{r}\times s^3$ saddles
abstract: gravitational path-integral over $\mathbb{r}\times s^3$ complex metrics with fluctuations is studied in 4d for einstein-hilbert gravity in lorentzian signature, with the aim to investigate the ir behaviour of complex saddles for various boundary choices. general covariance doesn't allow arbitrary boundary choices for the background and fluctuations. in the adm-decomposition, while imposing ``no-boundary'' condition at the initial boundary, two scenarios are considered for the final boundary: dirichlet and fixed extrinsic curvature. the universe undergoes a transition from a euclidean to a lorentzian phase in either scenario, where the dominant saddle in euclidean phase corresponds to a euclidean metric, while the lorentzian phase has two dominant complex saddles that superimpose. one-loop lapse action is computed using hurwitz-zeta regularization. uv-divergences canceled by suitable counterterms lead to a renormalized lapse action. one-loop hartle-hawking wave-function is computed using the picard-lefschetz (pl) and wkb methods, where the contributions from the metric fluctuations show secularly growing infrared divergences as the universe expands. this is compared with the situation in lorentzian ds, corresponding to a universe transitioning from an initial state of vanishing conjugate momenta to a final state of fixed extrinsic curvature. the pl method alone is not sufficient to overcome the technical hurdles in the one-loop computation, which needs to be supplemented by an $iε$-prescription, achieved via slight complexification of the cosmological constant $λ$. the renormalized one-loop ds wavefunction is seen to have qualitatively the same leading ir behaviour as the no-boundary wavefunction, though the coefficients are seen to be sensitive to the uv boundary choices. interestingly, for all boundary choices considered, the saddles remain ksw-allowed.

title: families of regular spacetimes and energy conditions
abstract: we present a systematic method for constructing static, spherically symmetric regular spacetimes of kerr-schild type in general relativity that satisfy the weak energy condition. our approach relies on physically reasonable assumptions on the matter energy density, together with the boundedness of the kretschmann scalar. the latter property ensures the finiteness of all curvature invariants and, for the configurations considered, is equivalent to the completeness of causal geodesics. by classifying admissible density profiles according to their complexity, we recover well-known regular black hole solutions such as the bardeen, hayward, and dymnikova models, which are thus naturally embedded in a unified and broader framework. within this setting, we also derive closed-form expressions for several new families of regular geometries involving hypergeometric or incomplete gamma functions, which in many cases reduce to elementary functions including algebraic, logarithmic, arctangent, and exponential forms. the emergence of horizons and photon spheres, as well as their observational implications, is also investigated. finally, we extend the analysis to rotating metrics generated through the newman-janis algorithm.

title: kerr/cft traversable wormhole with fermionic double-trace deformation
abstract: the construction of a traversable wormhole with double-trace deformation has been achieved so far by using boson fields as the perturbation. in this work, we study double-trace deformation with fermion fields in the two-sided kerr background to open a traversable wormhole. we construct the fermionic double-trace deformation within the kerr/cft framework. we consider the near-horizon, near-extremal kerr geometry, which is dual to a conformal field theory. the lack of fermionic superradiance let us describe the wormhole at every region, even at the off-axis region where bosonic field experiences instability due to superradiance. by choosing a certain coupling between the left and right boundaries, the two-point function is modified, and its first order correction contributes the negative energy to open the wormhole. the wormhole is most traversable when the perturbation is turned on at early times, with opening that depends on the mode's frequency, the black hole temperature, and the fermion mass. at late times, the average null energy has damped oscillation behavior until eventually reaches zero. wormhole with lower temperature have less traversability and it is completely closed at extreme limit. the same traversability can also be reproduced by using eikonal method. on the other hand, rotation and the number of fields involved in the deformation can increases the upper bound on information transfer up to the order of the entropy. additionally, symmetrical effective potential bumps connected by the wormhole can produce observable echoes. we find that the echo time delay cannot exceed the scrambling time of the black hole.

title: vacuum stability in geometric trinity of gravity
abstract: we investigate whether the classical equivalence of general relativity, its teleparallel equivalent, and its symmetric teleparallel equivalent extends to false-vacuum decay at leading semiclassical order. for a real scalar field minimally coupled to gravity, we compare the tunnelling exponent $b=s_{\rm b}-s_{\rm fv}$, which determines the exponential suppression of the decay rate, $γ\sim e^{-b}$, with the euclidean bounce, $s_{\rm b}$, and false-vacuum actions, $s_{\rm fv}$. the three formulations admit the same $o(4)$-symmetric coleman-de luccia bounce, but the boundary terms relating their actions can contribute to $b$. we explicitly evaluate the torsion and non-metricity boundary contributions at the regular origin, $r=0$, and at the asymptotic endpoint, $r\to\infty$. for regular configurations with consistently matched bounce and false-vacuum boundary data, these contributions vanish in both tegr and stegr. we therefore obtain $b_{\rm gr}=b_{\rm tegr}=b_{\rm stegr}$, establishing that the three formulations predict the same leading semiclassical suppression of false-vacuum decay within the class of configurations and boundary conditions considered.

title: additional observational signatures of asymmetric thin-shell wormholes within 4d einstein-gauss-bonnet gravity
abstract: in this paper, we study the optical appearance of a 4d einstein-gauss-bonnet asymmetric thin-shell wormhole. using visser's cut-and-paste construction, we determine the photon sphere radius and critical impact parameter for different values of the gauss-bonnet coupling $α$. we then investigate the effective potential and photon motion inside the wormhole spacetime. it is found that the effective potential, light ray paths, and azimuthal angle are closely tied to the mass ratio of the two spacetimes. considering an optically thin accretion disk as the only light source, we find that the asymmetric thin-shell wormhole's images exhibit additional photon rings and lensing bands that are absent for a 4d einstein-gauss-bonnet black hole. furthermore, the size of these extra rings increases with $α$, contrary to the black hole case. such exceptionally bright rings provide a reliable criterion for distinguishing and characterizing a thin-shell wormhole spacetime. we also verify that the mass ratio and throat radius significantly tune the morphology of these extra photon rings.

title: vishveshwara's waveform revisited: insights from a keldysh quasinormal mode expansion
abstract: we revisit vishveshwara's linear scattering on a schwarzschild black hole to study the evolution of quasinormal mode activation along the full time-domain waveform. specifically, by adopting a hyperboloidal approach we cast the scattering problem in a non-selfadjoint dynamics setting where a (keldysh) resonant expansion in a bi-orthogonal system of quasinormal modes can be readily performed. the calculation reveals the neat correlation of the second peak in vishveshwara's waveform to the fundamental mode and first overtones, closely following the ringdown waveform pattern of non-linear evolutions. the first peak is completely controlled, for even (zerilli) perturbations, by the algebraically special mode and the nearby branch cut. this phenomenon is absent for odd (regge-wheeler) perturbations. these qualitative features are robust under change of initial data, extending to reissner-nordström and kerr black holes but being absent when departing from asymptotic flatness to spacetime asymptotics without a branch cut. underlying linear mechanisms might shed light on the role of algebraic speciality in the transition to the ringdown in non-linear evolutions.

title: geometric capture and optical critical curves of purely electric, magnetic and dyonic black holes in einstein-euler-heisenberg theory
abstract: we examine background null capture in the electric, magnetic, and dyonic solutions of einstein gravity coupled to a quartic euler-heisenberg-type electromagnetic lagrangian. the calculation uses the exact hypergeometric electric solution, the closed-form magnetic solution, and a numerical dyonic solution. relative to the reissner-nordström value at fixed total charge, the eeh correction increases the geometric critical impact parameter in the parameter ranges considered. for the purely magnetic case, the disappearance of the two outer horizons can expose an additional capture barrier and thus forms an unstable circular orbit with a very small radius. in the dyonic case, for a fixed magnetic-to-electric charge ratio, the behavior is consistent with that of the pure electric solution while preserving the phase transition between single- and multi-horizon black hole phases. moreover, when the coupling parameter is fixed, the effect of the magnetic-to-electric charge ratio depends on the electric charge. the present findings establish that the multi-horizon phase can impart pronounced signatures to geometric photon observables, whereas, in the off-transition regime, the purely electric, purely magnetic, and dyonic solutions remain characterized by clearly distinguishable trends.

title: analytic and numerical study of dark matter halos in the horndeski theory
